# PACER (WACV 2027)

> PACER: Curriculum Self-Training with Spatial Uncertainty for Pseudo-Label Selection in Few-Shot Anatomical Landmark Detection. Roberto Di Via, Francesca Odone, Vito Paolo Pastore (MaLGa-DIBRIS, University of Genoa, Italy). IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV 2027).

PACER (Percentile-Adaptive Curriculum on Expected Radial Error) is a lightweight self-training stage that improves a pre-trained heatmap landmark detector using a few labeled radiographs and a larger unlabeled pool. It ranks unlabeled images by the Expected Radial Error (ERE), a label-free, millimeter-scale uncertainty read from the predicted heatmaps, and admits them as pseudo-labels through a percentile gate that expands an easy-to-hard curriculum. Because ERE is physically scaled, the gate needs no dataset-specific millimeter threshold and tightens in absolute terms as the detector sharpens.

Key results (5-shot, chest Shenzhen / cephalometric ISBI2015 / hand DHA):
- Improves 61 of 62 landmarks against the base it finetunes, concentrating on the hardest ones.
- On the CDPM-Align diffusion prior, MRE drops 4.14 -> 2.65 px (chest), 2.94 -> 2.19 mm (cephalometric), 4.19 -> 1.40 mm (hand).
- From the shared ImageNet base it is the best pool-only method on chest and cephalometric, about 6x faster than semi-supervised baselines.
